newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia allocates 5.1 bln rgt for infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia allocates 5.1 bln rgt for infrastructure.

text.p: Malaysia has proposed to allocate 5.1 billion ringgit for infrastructure and public amenities, Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said in his 1997 budget speech.

He said in Parliament that 2.9 billion ringgit will be set aside for roads and bridges, 889.5 million for rail transportation and the remainder for development of airports, water and electricity supply.
The capability and efficiency of ports are being continuously improved through the construction of multipurpose terminals at the ports of Johor, Bintulu and Klang, he said.

Anwar, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, said national power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd would reorganise its management in the transmission and distribution of electricity, while generation is to be undertaken jointly with the Independent Power Producers (IPPs).
Telekom Malaysia Bhd will modernise its main network systems through digital and diversified system for long-distance transmission.
Anwar also said the first phase of the Light Rail Transit (LRT) system, built to ease congestion in Kuala Lumpur, was expected to begin operation next month.
The Kuala Lumpur International Airport at Sepang, capable of handling 25 million passengers a year, would begin operations in early 1998.
